thread:
maya: Heads up — discovered cross-org rows showing up in the console insights table after the header-normalizer canary. Repro steps below.

maya: Steps: 1) hit /internal/insights with cookie auth for org A; 2) quick nav to dashboard; 3) observe a handful of rows from org B. Happens only on canary instances.

maya: Quick log snippet from canary pod: 
```
WARN header-normalizer: missing X-Org-Id, fallback to cookie org_id=org-A
INFO router: routed request to insights-handler (instance canary-3)
DEBUG metrics: quota_key resolved -> org-B (from cached header mapping)
```

sam.sre: oh no. Did the normalizer change header precedence? We used to prefer authenticated token org over cookie/header.

lina.prod: I think the new middleware strips X-Org-Id and canonicalizes to X-Org based on a best-effort cookie lookup. That sounds like it could mismatch when upstream proxy set X-Org for internal calls.

julian: if quota_key is derived from header post-normalization, and cookie fallback is allowed, race could pick stale mapping in cache. Any cached mapping TTL changes in the canary?

maya: Canary config had cache.ttl=60s (was 5s prod). We did that to reduce DB hits.

sam.sre: there’s the smoking gun. Longer TTL + header normalization that prefers cookie can lead to cross-org attribution during rapid org switches.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout step logs: canary-3 updated at 1748509120, header-normalizer:v2, cache.ttl=60s, traffic 12%

lina.prod: Immediate mitigation: rollback to header-normalizer:v1 or set cache.ttl back to 5s on canary. Also add strict invariant: if auth token present, force org_id from token and ignore cookie/header.

julian: agreed. Also we should add an assertion in telemetry tagging to include token-bound org_id and request_id so we can re-run queries to find affected user sessions.

maya: I'll open a quick PR to revert config and push a rollback. Can someone add an alert for org-scope mismatch metric (org_id != token_org_id)?

sam.sre: I'll add a temporary Grafana panel & alert. Query: count where telemetry.org != auth.org > 0 over 1m.

lina.prod: After rollback, we need a one-off job to scan recent telemetry to see how many dashboards/rows were exposed. Tag as P0 for CS notification if >50 sessions.

julian: For the longer fix: change normalizer to never down-prioritize token-derived org. Also remove cache keying by header mapping; use token-org as primary cache partition.

maya: rolling rollback now — will update when done.

deploy-bot: rollback started on canary group at 1748510200.

ops-bot: alert created: eng-platform/org-scope-mismatch, threshold=1, window=1m.

maya: rollback finished at 1748510345. Canary traffic back to v1. Initial checks: no cross-org rows seen on a quick sweep.

sam.sre: great. Follow-ups: 1) PR for normalizer invariant, 2) reduce TTL on mapping caches, 3) add regression test that simulates rapid org switching. I'll take 2 and 3.

lina.prod: I'll draft the PR for 1. Also pushing notes to runbook: "never rely solely on unauthenticated cookies for org resolution when token exists."

maya: thanks all. Filing postmortem stub and tagging CS for possible outreach.
